name: Underfloor Heating Mat
tagline: A fixed resistance laid in a mesh — the whole floor becomes the heater, slowly.
terminals: Cold tail — the mains lead that runs to the thermostat
Factory joint between the cold tail and the heating cable
Floor probe (sensor) leads — low voltage, to the thermostat
Earth braid or screen, bonded at the thermostat
parts: Heating cable — a series resistance in a fluoropolymer jacket
Fibreglass mesh backing — sets the spacing
Factory joint — the only joint allowed in the screed
Cold tail — the unheated lead back to the connection box
Floor temperature probe in its own conduit
safety: The mat is a fixed load buried in screed, so the insulation-resistance and continuity tests are done three times: before it is laid, after the screed goes down, and before it is tiled. Never cut the heating cable to shorten it — that changes the resistance and the wattage, and any joint buried in the floor will fail.

points.label: Fibreglass mesh backing
points.detail: The mesh is only a spacer: it holds the cable at a fixed pitch — usually 75 mm or 100 mm — so the floor heats evenly instead of in stripes. It is rolled out on the insulation board and cut (the mesh, never the cable) to turn corners.

points.label: Heating cable
points.detail: One continuous series resistance, so the mat's total wattage is fixed by its length: a 150 W/m² mat and a 200 W/m² mat look identical but are not interchangeable. The spacing you lay it at changes the heat per square metre, not the output of the cable.

points.label: Factory joint
points.detail: The transition from the heating cable to the plain mains cold tail, moulded and sealed at the factory. It is the only joint permitted in the floor, and it has to be fully embedded in the levelling compound — a joint left proud will crack the screed above it.

points.label: Cold tail and earth braid
points.detail: The unheated lead that runs up the wall to the thermostat or connection box. It carries the screen or earth braid that must be bonded at the thermostat end, because the thermostat and its RCD rely on that path to clear a cable damaged by a later fixing.

points.label: Floor temperature probe
points.detail: A thermistor in its own conduit laid between two cable runs, not touching them, so it reads the floor temperature rather than the cable's. The thermostat uses it to limit the floor surface to a safe temperature and to protect the floor covering — the probe, not the air sensor, is what stops a wood floor being cooked.
